summary: Stevens County, WA tower with an L-4 cab, built 1937 by the Resettlement Administration; staffed in 1940; destroyed or removed in the 1950s; footings remain.

facts.design: 45-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab on top
facts.status_note: Tower destroyed or removed in the 1950s (sources differ on the word); footings remain below the summit at the old lookout site per Willhite's photos

access.note: Reached by a hike on National Forest land from Sand Canyon Road and Major Road; Willhite's route notes are dated 2023 and describe an overgrown trail; no closure is described

visit.trail_note: Hike of 1.3 miles each way with about 600 feet of gain; old summit road is now an overgrown trail (Willhite, 2023 route notes)

events.note: Resettlement Administration built a 45-foot tower with an L-4 cab, per Willhite and the July 1937 Colville Examiner item
Lookouts installed on Cliff Ridge and Huckleberry Mountain as part of the Kaniksu ranger program (May 1939); a phone line was installed the same year
Kaniksu Forest Service placed Ray Bailey on the lookout
1950s (decade only). Willhite and firelookout.com say destroyed; the Register says removed
Registered December 14, 2012 as US 1490, WA 390; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Willhite and firelookout.com say the tower was destroyed in the 1950s; the Register says it was removed in the 1950s. The story reports the difference and does not choose.
The 1938 to 1940 sources name the Kaniksu National Forest, and the Register lists the site in the Colville National Forest today. The sources do not explain the change.

notes_for_editor: Brief's record (tower kind, 1,153.7 m, Stevens County, coordinates, 2012 FFLOS registration) matches the Register; no correction needed. Two searches found no fire records, so none are included. Access 'public' is inferred from a 2023 route description on National Forest land; the page describes no closure. The Forest Lookouts newspaper items are quoted from the Colville Examiner through that index, not from the newspaper itself.
